correctness.rationale: The dissipator is a completely positive trace-decreasing semigroup with no dark invariant subspace, giving finite integrated density. Its 9-real-variable resolvent yields the exact positive-denominator T(gamma). The identity T(gamma)-T(0)=gamma(6P-delta^2 kappa S)/(4P) reduces global superiority to minimization of G=6P/(kappa S); the sign polynomial K is quadratic with a single interior minimum if kappa^4<32 and no interior minimum otherwise. The separate derivative threshold has at most two positive roots, because the sign function R has R prime=12 kappa Q>0 wherever Q>0, proving uniqueness of the positive local minimum. Exact stationary/algebraic identities and independent 9x9 Liouvillian numerical checks passed.

value.rationale: A single local dephasing control has a global phase diagram with exact detuning cost, optimizer multiplicity at coexistence, and a sharp switch from finite-jump onset to continuous onset. This resolves a natural transport-time engineering decision across all positive capture rates and real detunings, beyond a routine finite calculation or an isolated special parameter. The model assumptions and lack of experimental guarantees are explicit.
